body.estimand_functional: On the relevant-component cycle-rank-at-most-one class, let \(C_X,C_Y\) be the weak components of \(X,Y\).  Then \(C^\star(I)=+\infty\) if \(C_X\ne C_Y\), and, for \(C_X=C_Y=C\), \(C^\star(I)=+\infty\) when \(C\) has cycle rank zero and \(X\not\leadsto_{G[C]}Y\); \(C^\star(I)=\min_{s_i\in R(P_i)\setminus\{a_{P_i}\}}\sum_{i=1}^m C_i(s_{i-1},s_i)\) when \(C\) has cycle rank zero and \(X\leadsto_{G[C]}Y\); and \(C^\star(I)=\operatorname{MS}_1(I|_C)\) when \(C\) has cycle rank one.  In every branch, existence is equivalent to \(C^\star(I)<+\infty\)

sampling_model.design: No statistical sampling; the input is one explicitly encoded finite acyclic NSCM and one designated actual solution.
sampling_model.units: Vertices, domain values, local-table rows, output incidences, graph edges, and rational cost records counted by \(L\).
sampling_model.treatment: The singleton counterfactual intervention changes \(X=a_X\) to some \(X=x'\ne a_X\).
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; local tables are total and all finite domains are explicitly enumerated.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None; the local relations are supplied exactly rather than estimated.

body.tldr: Beckers defines actual causation by counterfactual dependence in an actualized structural simplification, but the definition itself gives no exact algorithmic frontier. Under finite explicit local tables, the project proves a relevant-component frontier: the answer is immediately negative when \(X\) and \(Y\) lie in different weak full-graph components; otherwise arbitrary unrelated components are harmless, and an exact certificate calculus is polynomial whenever their common component has cycle rank at most one. A rank-zero component first yields a directed-reachability cut when \(X\) cannot reach \(Y\), and only a reachable instance invokes the linear-arithmetic value-path compiler; a rank-one component uses the exceptional-edge min-sum program. The backend returns a witness and exact optimum certificate or a separating cut. A shared-selector construction separately proves NP-completeness even for deterministic binary models whose endogenous graph is one directed chain, showing why the positive full-graph restriction is substantive.

project_justification.gap: Section 6, Proposition 20 on page 525, with proof on page 532, of Beckers2025Actual supplies a same-signature structural-simplification representative but no compiler, certificate system, minimum-cost result, or complexity classification. Existing causal-tree algorithms and SAT encodings concern Halpern--Pearl causation and do not enforce Beckers's full-graph reachability legality or actual-row freezing.
project_justification.niche: The novel computational scope uses finite explicitly encoded tables and restricts only the weak full-graph component relevant to \(X\) and \(Y\): disconnected queries are rejected by a component cut, while a common component of cycle rank zero or one is tractable even if every other component is unrestricted. This is a full-graph condition on \(U\cup V\), not the published endogenous causal-tree condition for Halpern--Pearl causation.
project_justification.fill: The project proves component restriction with cost preservation, an explicit three-way frontier functional, a linear-arithmetic value-path compiler after a directed-reachability test, and an exact exceptional-edge min-sum algorithm for a connected rank-one component. Independently checkable positive, optimality, and negative certificates accompany the result. The restricted chain reduction and shared-selector obstruction establish the complementary Beckers hardness phenomenon without claiming unrestricted counting or general treewidth tractability.

body.related_work: Beckers2025Actual, Section 5.1, Definitions 13, 15, and 16 on pages 523--524 and Section 6, Definitions 18 and 19 and Proposition 20 on page 525, supplies the structural-simplification and actual-causation semantics implemented here; the proof of Proposition 20 appears on page 532. It contains neither a compiler nor the relevant-component complexity frontier. Beckers2025NCM supplies set-valued equations and topological counterfactual semantics, while finite explicit encoding is this project's computational-scope restriction. The earlier UAI version of EiterLukasiewicz2006Tractable, Section 4.1 and Theorems 4.2--4.3, is the closest methodological comparator: its Halpern--Pearl causal-tree analysis propagates subsets of endogenous path-variable domains. The present positive theorem instead audits Beckers actualized projection and deletion legality on the full graph, first separating directed nonreachability in a forest component and then extending exact computation through one full-graph cycle by an exceptional-edge state. The shared-selector proposition shows only that transferring the unaugmented endogenous-only state type loses full-exogenous reachability information; it does not modify the published Halpern--Pearl theorem. EiterLukasiewicz2002Complexity and AleksandrowiczEtAl2014 show that complexity depends on the causation definition, but neither treats Beckers deletion. IbrahimRehwaldPretschner2019SAT and IbrahimPretschner2020Optimization address Boolean Halpern--Pearl encodings and objectives, and ReydDiaconescuDessalles2025Search gives approximate Halpern--Pearl-style search; none supplies the arbitrary-domain exact Beckers certificates proved here.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The positive theorem requires finite explicitly indexed local tables and that the common weak full-graph component of \(X\) and \(Y\) have cycle rank at most one; it makes no claim for relevant components of larger cycle rank, general full-graph treewidth, succinct mechanisms, continuous domains, or negative deletion costs. The hardness theorem concerns a broader Beckers class described by an endogenous chain and shared exogenous selectors, not the positive relevant-component class. The selector reduction gives a bijection only for normalized certificates; unrestricted successful retained graphs need not be counted parsimoniously.
body.honest_scope: The exact tractability statement is component-local: different weak components give a negative answer, and when \(X\) and \(Y\) share a component, all other components may be retained at their actual assignments regardless of their cycle structure. A common rank-zero component is split again by full directed reachability; no path means value \(+\infty\), whereas a path activates the unique-path functional. A common rank-one component is handled by the proved normalized min-sum functional and exceptional-edge legality modes. These are restrictions on the full graph over \(U\cup V\), not assumptions inherited from Beckers or the endogenous causal-tree class of Eiter--Lukasiewicz. The explicit-table, finite-domain, acyclic, total-table, actual-solution, and nonnegative-rational-cost conditions remain in force. No general treewidth fixed-parameter algorithm or unrestricted parsimonious certificate-counting theorem is claimed.
